primitives.name: Calibration-Honest vs Edge-Empty
primitives.verbatim_quote: Calibration-honest vs edge-empty.** ECE 0.0044 / Brier 0.2556 (solved) vs R*≈-0.0057 / MI 0.0095 nats p=0.060 (empty).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'ECE': 'Expected Calibration Error (dimensionless)', 'Brier': 'Brier Score (dimensionless)', 'R*': 'Relative Calibration Score (dimensionless)', 'MI': 'Mutual Information (nats)'}
primitives.assumptions: The model's calibration is evaluated independently of its predictive edge; adversarial resolution requires distinguishing between calibrated honesty and empty edge.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When mutual information is below threshold (p=0.060), the model is considered to have empty edge despite apparent calibration.

layer2.mapping: GSI's calibration layer maps to a dual inference space where ECE/Brier scores are resolved against R*/MI metrics; the resolution is adversarial, not just statistical.
layer2.telemetry: ECE, Brier, R*, MI values from validation set

primitives.name: Market Consensus vs Late Steam
primitives.verbatim_quote: Market consensus vs late steam.** High book-consensus games are where the engine underperforms most (36.3% on-ladder); late odds-path moves carry ~14× the return association of cross-sectional final odds.
primitives.assumptions: Late odds-path moves are more informative than static consensus; the engine underperforms when consensus is high.
primitives.breakdown_regime: High consensus games exhibit low on-ladder performance and reduced signal from static odds.

layer2.mapping: GSE's late-move kernel encodes velocity of odds path as a signal strength metric; this is derived from the difference between static consensus and dynamic path evolution.
layer2.telemetry: Late-move velocity, cross-sectional odds, on-ladder accuracy

primitives.name: Sim-to-Real
primitives.verbatim_quote: Sim-to-real.** ForecastBench-sim ρ=+0.43 (ρ2≈0.185 — a signal, not a certificate).
primitives.assumptions: Simulated forecasts correlate with real-world outcomes, but the correlation is not deterministic or certifying.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Correlation is a signal, not a guarantee; simulation must be version-controlled and validated.

layer2.mapping: GSI's sim-to-real mapping aligns simulated forecast distributions with real-world outcomes using a version-locked simulator and rubric scoring.
layer2.telemetry: ρ, ρ², version-locked simulator hash, rubric score

Calibration-honest vs edge-empty is resolved by ensuring that the model's calibration is not conflated with its edge; the resolution hinges on the distinction between ECE/Brier and R*/MI. Market consensus vs late steam is resolved by recognizing that static consensus is noise while dynamic path evolution carries signal; this is formalized through a velocity-based kernel in GSE. Sim-to-real is resolved by enforcing version-locking and rubric scoring to ensure that simulations are not treated as certificates but as signals. These primitives are not independent but form a dual inference architecture where each resolves a contradiction in the others.
